messages:
frank: quick PSA from today's onboarding run: demo servers didn't pick up rotated keys in our container images. repro and notes below.

sara: thanks — can you paste a minimal repro? this sounds like the env-vs-file precedence issue.

frank: repro:
```
# cluster: secret mounted as file /etc/creds/redwood -> app exposes REDWOOD_TOKEN via downward API
# console: rotate API key -> new REDWOOD_API_KEY available
kubectl rollout restart deploy/demo
# after restart: app logs: 'using token from /etc/creds/redwood (old)'
```
we also had RW_PROJECT and REDWOOD_ORG set in different places, which made resolution weird for cross-account calls.

priya: two things jumping out: 1) inconsistent precedence across runtimes (some SDKs treat file > env), 2) credential cache doesn't detect file-content changes or env value swaps on restart when legacy aliases are present.

sara: what env names are in play here? we've got REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_TOKEN (legacy), RW_LEGACY_KEY, plus org/project vars: REDWOOD_ORG and RW_PROJECT. docs have been fuzzy about which wins.

frank: current observed behavior across services: C++ runtime prefers file -> REDWOOD_TOKEN -> REDWOOD_API_KEY; Node prefers REDWOOD_API_KEY -> REDWOOD_TOKEN -> file. total chaos.

priya: proposed unified ruleset (RFC suggestion):
- resolution order: 1) explicit org-scoped env (REDWOOD_ORG + REDWOOD_API_KEY-org) 2) REDWOOD_API_KEY (primary) 3) REDWOOD_TOKEN (legacy) 4) RW_LEGACY_KEY 5) credential file/cache
- if both REDWOOD_API_KEY and any legacy alias are present, prefer REDWOOD_API_KEY and emit a WARN that legacy var is deprecated with a link to migration guide
- if REDWOOD_ORG is set, require org-scoped key; if not found, warn and fall back with explicit event.

sara: love that. also recommend shipping a tiny shared resolver library (js/py/go bindings) so behaviors are identical. keep resolver pure and tiny so SDKs can vendor it.

frank: cache behavior: implement a cheap fingerprint check on startup for file-backed creds (sha256 of first 512 bytes) and compare to cached fingerprint; if differ, invalidate cache and reload. also support env-value diff to detect rotation when the env var changed.

priya: for runtime ergonomics: add signal handling + API: SIGHUP -> reload creds (unix), and export client.reloadCredentials() for Windows processes. tie CLI flag `--reload-creds` to the same codepath. emit telemetry event `cred.reload` with reason=signal|cli|api.

sara: good to include guidance for containers: recommend using env injection for short-lived tokens or annotated restart on secret change (k8s rollout or use external controller). document caveats of Downward API mounts.

frank: tests: unit tests for resolver precedence matrix, integration that simulates secret rotation via file rewrite and process restart, and cross-language compatibility tests using the shared resolver package. add e2e where we simulate RW_PROJECT/REDWOOD_ORG combos to ensure correct scoping.

priya: telemetry: add fields `cred.source` (env|file|legacy) and `cred.deprecated_alias=true/false` so we can measure migration. patch our analytics to surface high-usage legacy vars monthly.

sara: docs: short-term add a Quickstart appendix called "Credential precedence & rotation" with examples for local dev, k8s Downward API, secret mounts, and recommended signal patterns. assign to docs-bot to create ticket.

docs-bot: created DOCS-5200 "Credential precedence & rotation guide" and assigned to @maria-docs.

frank: implementation owners: priya to prototype resolver package + fingerprint check, sara to wire signal/reload into node sdk and sample-app, i'll run integration tests in our k8s smoke cluster.

sara: we'll also add a runtime warning at startup when multiple conflicting env keys are present that prints chosen source and a short migration link. keep it low-noise.

priya: follow-up: I'll open RFC draft and prototype repo `redwood/creds-shared` with JS + Python shims. will include README with migration steps and deprecation timeline.

bot-deploy: CI triggered for branch feat/cred-unify (#3210). matrix will run node/py/go tests.

frank: thanks folks. if we get this in next sprint it should cut down a bunch of support tickets and make rotations predictable for demos and customers. ping me for early review. :handshake:
